30 The electric current in a metal wire is 4.0 mA.
How many electrons pass a fixed point in the wire in a time of 10 hours?
A
2.5  1017
B
2.5  1020
C
9.0  1020
D
9.0  1023

hints: Convert the given $4.0\text{ mA}$ to amperes and the given 10 hours to seconds before using any electricity equation.
Recall that current is rate of flow of charge, $I = Q/t$, and each electron carries magnitude $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
First calculate $Q = It$ in coulombs, then calculate $N = Q/e$ and check the power of 10 carefully.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: $I = 4.0\text{ mA} = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}$ and $t = 10\text{ hours} = 10 \times 3600\text{ s} = 36000\text{ s}$.
Use current as charge per unit time: $I = Q/t$, so total charge past the point is $Q = It$.
Substitute values with units: $Q = (4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A})(36000\text{ s}) = 144\text{ C}$.
Relate charge to number of electrons using elementary charge $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$: $Q = Ne$, so $N = Q/e$.
This matches $9.0 \times 10^{20}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This uses $t = 10\text{ s}$ instead of 10 hours, giving $Q = 0.04\text{ C}$ and about $2.5 \times 10^{17}$ electrons.

B.explanation: This is too small by a factor of about 3.6, consistent with a wrong hours-to-seconds conversion such as taking 1 hour as $1000\text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Total charge $Q = It = 144\text{ C}$ divided by $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ gives $N = 9.0 \times 10^{20}$ electrons.

D.explanation: This uses $4.0\text{ A}$ instead of $4.0\text{ mA}$, so the charge and electron number are 1000 times too large.
